A1.justification: All 11 pages of each PDF are readable and describe the same Retinex-MEF study. The methods, equations, experiments, figures and tables can be matched reliably. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, although both refer to separate supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SICE and MEFB evaluations, exposure-control and extreme-exposure demonstrations, and loss-function ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–10.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original quantitative evaluations, qualitative demonstrations and ablation results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–10.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same three modules, auxiliary-image sampling, five training losses and controllable illumination-fusion procedure. Revised explanations and the formal glare-bound correction do not establish an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions train on SICE and evaluate on SICE and MEFB. Mixed-exposure fusion, exposure adjustment, and fusion of pairs that are both underexposed or both overexposed remain the same evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 5 and 8 retain CUNet, SDNet, DeFusion, CRMEF, DDMEF, MEFLUT and FILM as comparators. Newly cited methods such as RDGMEF and DMEF are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain 300 SICE training sequences, 100 SICE test pairs, 30 MEFB pairs, 80 training epochs, Adam with batch size 8, and the same learning-rate schedule, loss weights and exposure controls. Table 2 changes its 'MEF' column label to 'SSIM', consistent with the existing setup and Table 1; the evidence supports a labeling correction rather than a changed metric.

E4.justification: The same five loss ablations and the same exposure-control, extreme-exposure and decomposition analyses appear in both versions. Section 4.6 revises their explanation, but Table 2 and Figures 7–10 introduce no new experimental controls or analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both tables continue to report individual metric values without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All 96 numerical entries in Table 1 and all 36 entries in Table 2 are identical. The empirical image panels, method rankings and reported performance trends are also retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the assumption G > 0 to G >= 0, explicitly permitting zero glare. The expanded symmetry explanation in Section 3.4 introduces a sign inconsistency: it describes two signed brightness differences as equal although the retained symmetry identity makes them opposite in sign. The remaining mathematics is unchanged apart from renaming the ideal reflectance.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the explicit description of producing an HDR image with the narrower description of producing a well-exposed, high-quality composite. The central contributions—unsupervised shared-reflectance recovery, glare mitigation and controllable exposure fusion—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 now explicitly interprets ablation I as reducing the model to traditional Retinex decomposition, explaining its whitish color cast; v1 described color degradation more generally. Other result interpretations are retained, and no substantive new limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces v1's promise that code will be released with a statement of availability and a concrete HaowenBai/Retinex-MEF repository address. Hardware, implementation descriptions and hyperparameter disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Citation coverage expands substantially to additional Retinex fusion, multimodal and video fusion, and image/video coding research. Section 3.4 newly attributes illumination adjustment to earlier curve-based enhancement work, while Section 2.2 explicitly names the already-cited PairLIE as a foundation. References to Palsson's multispectral fusion work and Shao's halo-free fusion work are removed. These changes extend beyond bibliographic renumbering.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, method opening, exposure-function explanation and ablation narrative undergo substantial rewriting. MEIF is standardized to MEF, contribution bullets are reordered, and acknowledgements and an additional corresponding-author marker are added. The overall section hierarchy remains stable.

P2.justification: Both retain ten figures and two tables. v2 redraws the loss schematic in Figure 4 and symmetry illustration in Figure 6, explicitly annotates illumination averaging in Figure 3, and adjusts labels, spacing and captions. Table 2's metric header is corrected to SSIM; the empirical displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: Clearer prose and explanatory diagrams, the corrected SSIM label and glare bound, and concrete code-access information modestly improve clarity and usability. Empirical support remains unchanged. The gains are tempered by the new symmetry sign inconsistency in Section 3.4 and added coding citations whose connection to the introduction's MEF supervision claim is unclear.
